brief: Tonight is Legs B, and it is a longer night than the last one you ran. The hip abductor and the hip adductor both landed on this day after you accepted them, so Legs B goes from six lifts to eight for the first time. Budget the time before you start rather than discovering it at the end. The one real change is the Romanian deadlift: it is three sets tonight, not four. Here is the honest reason, because the half-version of it would be a lie. On 16 August you wrote asking whether four sets of leg curls on RDL day was too much hamstring work, and that same night the card asked you for four RDL sets and you did three. You answered your own question with your feet. The leg curl did come down from four sets to three when you accepted that change on 23 August — but on its own that fixed nothing, because three RDL plus four curls was seven hamstring sets, and four RDL plus three curls is seven again. Same number, rearranged. Cutting the fourth RDL set is what actually drops the night to six. What that costs you is real and you should know it: the three RDL weights tonight are the exact three you lifted on 16 August, so your hinge does not move this session. The progression trainer wanted the opposite — 205 for ten off the back of two nines, on 30 July and 16 August — and it was not wrong about the number, it was wrong about the night. If all three finish clean, the next Legs B opens at 205 for ten. Everything else steps by one rep, which is the smallest honest move there is: leg press holds 180 and closes 12, 12, 11 instead of fading to ten; the leg curl earns its jump to 150 outright, after four sets of twelve at 142.5 on the 16th and thirteens on the 20th, so it opens at ten reps, the bottom of the range; hips go to 14 and 13; calves 14, 13, 13; crunches 14 across; hanging leg raises 13 and 13. On conditioning, nothing has been logged, and you are twenty-seven weeks out. Ten to fifteen minutes of steady cardio after the last set is the cheapest thing on this list.

Straight about the cost: the three RDL weights tonight are exactly what you lifted on 16 August, so your hinge does not move this session. If all three finish clean, the next Legs B opens at 205 for ten.

Finishing your 16 August question properly. Dropping the leg curl to three sets did not actually reduce anything — three RDL plus four curls was seven sets, four RDL plus three curls is seven again. Cutting the fourth RDL set is what takes tonight down to six.

Tonight is the longest Legs B you have run: eight lifts, not six. The hip abductor and hip adductor you accepted both appear on this day for the first time. If the clock beats you, those two hip sets come out — not the RDL.
Your 23 August question about lateral raises is a card tonight. The answer is no, four is not right for that muscle, and the card cuts Push B to the three sets you actually did.
Meso 2 opened on 24 August. This is week 1 of 4, a build block, so the next three weeks add work before anything comes back off.

Still open and I still cannot put it on a card: every core set you do bends you forward, and there is no anti-rotation movement like a Pallof press anywhere in the app exercise list, so it cannot be prescribed until that list is changed. Say the word and it gets added.

proposals.why: You asked on 23 August whether four sets is right for such a small muscle group, and the answer is no — Push B already opens with four sets of overhead press and Push A adds three cable lateral raises on top, so this makes it the three sets you actually did that night, all of them at fifteen reps.

The cable reverse curl asks twelve to fifteen reps and your last five Pull B nights have never once put a set above twelve — eleven, eleven, eleven at 37.5 on both 15 and 25 August — so the weight can never move, and asking ten to twelve makes the twelves you already did in July the thing that earns the next step.

dissent.progression: Four sets — 155 and 185 for ten, then 205 for ten and 205 for nine; two top sets of 205 for nine, on 30 July and 16 August, have earned the tenth rep.
dissent.recovery: Three sets at the exact weights he lifted on 16 August — he was asked for four that night, did three, and wrote his hamstring-volume question the same evening.
dissent.why: Progression is right about the number and wrong about the night, and I want that said plainly rather than buried. 205 for nine twice does earn 205 for ten; I am not pretending otherwise, and the packet says so on his card. But three facts sit against running it tonight. First, he asked this question in writing on 16 August and answered it with his feet on the same session — asked for four, did three. That is one man saying the same thing twice, and this app has a history of reading past him. Second, and this is the one that decided it: the change he accepted on 23 August did not do what it looked like it did. Cutting leg curl from four sets to three took the night from three RDL plus four curls to four RDL plus three curls — seven hamstring sets either way. Had I ruled for progression, the app would have printed the same seven sets he questioned while separately telling him his question had been addressed. A card that contradicts its own stated reason is the exact failure this repo was burned by twice, and it outranks a single earned rep. Third, tonight is the longest Legs B he has ever run — the hip abductor and adductor both land on this day for the first time, taking it from six lifts to eight — so this is the wrong night to add a set to his heaviest hinge. I took recovery whole, including its weights, which means the hinge does not progress tonight; that cost is stated on the card and in the flags rather than hidden, and the next Legs B opens at 205 for ten if all three sets finish clean. Recovery filed no veto, so this was mine to decide, not a seat overruled.

overrides.reason: Three sets tonight, not four. On 16 August the card asked you for four and you did three, and that same night you wrote asking whether the hamstring work on this day was too much — you answered your own question with your feet. Dropping the leg curl to three sets did not fix it on its own: three RDL plus four curls was seven sets and four RDL plus three curls is seven again. Cutting this set is what takes the night to six. The weights are exactly what you lifted on 16 August, so nothing moves here tonight; if all three finish clean the next Legs B opens at 205 for ten.

On 16 August you went 12, then 11, then 10 — you faded across the three sets. The card would print 180 for twelve three times, which asks a two-rep jump on the set that has been fading. The weight holds and the back end closes instead: 12, 12, 11. The next pin on this machine is 200 and it opens when all three sets reach twelve.

You carried 142.5 for four straight sets of twelve on 16 August, the top of the range on every set, which earns the step to 150 outright — and four days later you took the same 142.5 for thirteen twice on Legs A, so that weight has nothing left to give you. Ten reps is the bottom of the range and the honest place to land the night after a step up. This is also three sets now, not four, which is the change you asked for on 16 August.

First time this lift appears on Legs B since you accepted it. The card would open lighter at 127.5 and then jump to 135, both for fifteen — dropping the opening weight and pasting the top of the range on at the same time. You did 135 for thirteen twice on 20 August, up from twelve and twelve on 2 August, so the weight holds and one more rep on each set is the step. Fifteen on both buys 142.5.

Also its first appearance on this day. The card would print 105 for twelve twice, which is your 20 August sets copied across word for word and asks you for nothing. You moved up to 105 that night off fifteens at 97.5 and landed at twelve and twelve, the bottom of the range. Thirteen on both is the next rung, and fifteens open 112.5.

The card asks fifteen on all three sets at 300, which is three more reps than your last set has ever managed at that load. You went 12, 12, 12 on 16 August and 13, 13, 12 on 20 August, so one more rep on the opener and one on the closer is the real step. The next platform load is 320 and it opens when 300 goes fifteen across.

Three sets of thirteen at 60 on 20 August, up from three sets of twelve at the same weight on 16 August. The card prints fifteen across, two more reps per set than you have done here. Fourteen is the single-rep step, and fifteen across is what buys 65.

Bodyweight, so reps are the only thing that can move. The card prints twelve and twelve — the same pair it printed on 30 July and 16 August, and actually less than you already did on 20 August when you opened with thirteen. Thirteen on both is the step, and the range runs to fifteen.
